original_query: select l_orderkey, sum(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) as revenue, o_orderdate, o_shippriority from customer, orders, lineitem where c_mktsegment = 'MACHINERY' and c_custkey = o_custkey and l_orderkey = o_orderkey and o_orderdate < date '1995-03-20' and l_shipdate > date '1995-03-20' group by l_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_shippriority order by revenue desc, o_orderdate limit 10;
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    o.o_orderkey AS l_orderkey,
    SUM(l.l_extendedprice * (1 - l.l_discount)) AS revenue,
    o.o_orderdate,
    o.o_shippriority
FROM customer c
JOIN orders o ON c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey
JOIN lineitem l ON l.l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey
WHERE c.c_mktsegment = 'MACHINERY'
  AND o.o_orderdate < DATE '1995-03-20'
  AND l.l_shipdate > DATE '1995-03-20'
GROUP BY o.o_orderkey, o.o_orderdate, o.o_shippriority
ORDER BY revenue DESC, o.o_orderdate
LIMIT 10;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Convert implicit comma joins to explicit INNER JOINs for clarity; semantics unchanged.
Predicates are already simple and selective; no redundant predicates to remove.
No subqueries exist, so CTEs are unnecessary and may add materialization overhead; avoid them.
Best plan drives from the selective customer->orders set into lineitem; this is achieved mainly through indexing rather than SQL reordering, which the optimizer controls.
